types.embedding_query_text: Month: A calendar month. Also called month period, monthly period. Examples: February 2022.

candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. candidates.label: Season

Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: Distance: The amount of space between two points. Also called length, gap. Examples: 1,300km, 700km, 808 miles, 435 miles.

candidates.label: Distance

candidates.label: Quantity

candidates.label: Place

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A number or amount of something. Also called count, number. Examples: 93 drones, 605 Ukrainian drones, four fires.

candidates.label: Quantity

Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Energy

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A collection of people or things. Also called set, bunch. Examples: four people, 11 people, three people, two people.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: Four people and 11 people are quantities, matching Quantity.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A proportion expressed as a fraction of 100. Also called percent, share. Examples: 25%, 31%, 69%.

chosen_type.label: Float
chosen_type.justification: 25%, 31%, 69% are percentages, which are floats, matching Float.

candidates.label: Float
candidates.comment: Float is a Number data type representing a floating-point number. Also called decimal number, real number. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0, 2.718.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValueDistribution is a StructuredValue representing a statistical distribution of values. Also called value distribution, statistical range. Examples: the average height of a population with standard deviation, a product's price distribution across different retailers, a range of test scores with median and mode.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration

types.embedding_query_text: Ship: A large watercraft. Also called vessel, boat. Examples: two dry cargo ships.

candidates.label: BoatTrip

Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: BoatReservation

candidates.label: Canal

types.embedding_query_text: Facility: A place or structure designed for a specific purpose. Also called site, installation. Examples: drone storage sites.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment

types.embedding_query_text: Phenomenon: An observable occurrence or event. Also called occurrence, event. Examples: smoke plumes.

types.embedding_query_text: GeographicFeature: A natural or man-made feature of the Earth's surface. Also called landform, terrain feature. Examples: front line.

candidates.label: Mountain

Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

candidates.label: GeoShape
candidates.comment: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater

Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Continent
